banking_vn.v5: NPL (Non-Performing Loan) classification in Vietnam follows SBV Circular 11/2021: Group 1 (current, ≤10 days overdue, 0% provision), Group 2 (special mention, 11-90 days, 5%), Group 3 (substandard, 91-180 days, 20%), Group 4 (doubtful, 181-360 days, 50%), Group 5 (loss, >360 days, 100%). Banks must classify and provision monthly. NPL ratio target is <3%.
banking_vn.v6: Loan (NPL) classification in Vietnam follows SBV Circular 31/2024, which replaced Circular 11/2021: Group 1 (current, under 10 days overdue, 0% provision), Group 2 (special mention, 10 to under 90 days, 5%), Group 3 (substandard, 90 to under 180 days, 20%), Group 4 (doubtful, 180 to under 360 days, 50%), Group 5 (loss, 360 days or more, 100%). Banks must classify and provision monthly. NPL ratio target is <3%.

banking_vn.v5: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) in Vietnam per SBV Circular 22/2019: minimum 8% = (Tier 1 + Tier 2 Capital) / Risk-Weighted Assets. Other key ratios: short-term capital for medium/long-term lending ≤30%, single customer exposure ≤15% of equity, related party exposure ≤5% of equity, LCR ≥100%.
banking_vn.v6: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) in Vietnam per SBV Circular 41/2016: minimum 8% = (Tier 1 + Tier 2 Capital) / Risk-Weighted Assets. Circular 22/2019 ratios: short-term capital for medium/long-term lending ≤30%, loan-to-deposit ≤85%, liquidity reserve ≥10%, a 30-day solvency ratio, related party exposure ≤5% of equity. Law 32/2024 caps single-customer exposure at 13% of equity in 2026 (10% from 2029).

Under the 2022 AML Law an STR is due within 3 working days of the transaction or of detecting it, not 48 hours.

banking_vn.v5: eKYC in Vietnam per TT16/2020: requires CCCD chip reading (NFC), facial recognition matching (>95% confidence), liveness detection, OTP verification. Three account tiers: Tier 1 (basic, limited transactions), Tier 2 (standard, video eKYC), Tier 3 (full, advanced eKYC or branch visit). Digital banking features include VietQR payments, Napas 24/7 transfers, mobile banking.
banking_vn.v6: eKYC in Vietnam per Circular 17/2024: requires chip ID card reading (NFC), facial recognition matching, liveness detection and OTP verification; from 1 January 2025 accounts without biometrics matched to the chip ID cannot transact online. Decision 2345/QĐ-NHNN requires biometric authentication for online transfers above VND 10 million or VND 20 million a day. Accounts opened by eKYC carry transaction limits. Digital banking features include VietQR payments, Napas 24/7 transfers, mobile banking.
banking_vn.why: Circular 17/2024/TT-NHNN (payment accounts, eKYC with the chip ID card) and Decision 2345/QD-NHNN (biometric checks on online transfers) replaced Circular 16/2020's account rules from 1 July 2024.

banking_vn.v5: Vietnamese banking handoff chain: eKYC → Account Opening (5 min SLA). Loan Application → CIC Check → Credit Analysis → Legal → Disbursement. banking_vn_T1.v5: SBV Circular 11/2021 (Thông tư 11/2021/TT-NHNN) classifies loans into 5 groups: Group 1 (Current) — overdue ≤10 days, provision 0%; Group 2 (Special Mention) — overdue 11-90 days, provision 5%; Group 3 (Substandard) — overdue 91-180 days, provision 20%; Group 4 (Doubtful) — overdue 181-360 days, provision 50%; Group 5 (Loss) — overdue >360 days, provision 100%. NPL ratio (Groups 3-5) target is <3%.

banking_vn_T2.v5: Define CAR, LCR, and NSFR as required by SBV Circular 22/2019 for Vietnamese banks.
banking_vn_T2.v6: Define CAR, LCR and NSFR, and explain which of them SBV rules require Vietnamese banks to meet.
banking_vn_T2.why: The 8% CAR minimum comes from Circular 41/2016/TT-NHNN (Basel II), not Circular 22/2019. The SBV has not made Basel III LCR or NSFR a legal minimum; Circular 22/2019 sets a liquidity reserve ratio of at least 10%, a 30-day solvency ratio and a loan-to-deposit cap of 85%.

banking_vn_T2.v5: CAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio / Tỷ lệ an toàn vốn) = (Tier 1 + Tier 2 Capital) / Risk-Weighted Assets, minimum 8% per SBV. LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio / Tỷ lệ bao phủ thanh khoản) = High-Quality Liquid Assets / Total Net Cash Outflows over 30 days, minimum 100%. NSFR (Net Stable Funding Ratio / Tỷ lệ nguồn vốn ổn định ròng) = Available Stable Funding / Required Stable Funding, minimum 100%. All ratios are mandated by SBV Circular 22/2019/TT-NHNN as part of Vietnam's Basel III adoption.
banking_vn_T2.v6: CAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio / Tỷ lệ an toàn vốn) = (Tier 1 + Tier 2 Capital) / Risk-Weighted Assets; the SBV requires at least 8% under Circular 41/2016 (Basel II). LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio / Tỷ lệ bao phủ thanh khoản) = High-Quality Liquid Assets / Total Net Cash Outflows over 30 days, and NSFR (Net Stable Funding Ratio / Tỷ lệ nguồn vốn ổn định ròng) = Available Stable Funding / Required Stable Funding; both are Basel III measures with a 100% benchmark that banks may track internally, but the SBV has not made them legal minimums. Instead SBV Circular 22/2019 requires a liquidity reserve ratio of at least 10%, a 30-day solvency ratio and a loan-to-deposit ratio of at most 85%.

banking_vn_T6.v5: The deposit of VND 450 million exceeds the cash transaction reporting threshold of VND 400 million per Nghị định 116/2013/NĐ-CP. The bank must: (1) File a Cash Transaction Report (CTR) with AMLD (Cục Phòng chống rửa tiền), (2) Verify customer identity through CDD, (3) Document the source of funds, (4) Screen against sanctions lists (UN, OFAC, SBV domestic list). If the pattern suggests structuring or is inconsistent with the customer profile, an STR must also be filed within 48 hours.
banking_vn_T6.v6: The deposit of VND 450 million exceeds the large-value cash transaction reporting threshold of VND 400 million set under the 2022 AML Law (Luật PCRT 2022) by Decision 11/2023/QĐ-TTg, with Decree 19/2023/NĐ-CP. The bank must: (1) File a large-value transaction report (CTR) with AMLD (Cục Phòng chống rửa tiền), (2) Verify customer identity through CDD, (3) Document the source of funds, (4) Screen against sanctions lists (UN, OFAC, SBV domestic list). If the pattern suggests structuring or is inconsistent with the customer profile, an STR must also be filed within 3 working days.
banking_vn_T6.why: The 2022 AML Law (Law 14/2022/QH15, in force 1 March 2023) and Decree 19/2023/ND-CP replaced Decree 116/2013; Decision 11/2023/QD-TTg now sets the VND 400 million large-value threshold. Under the 2022 AML Law an STR is due within 3 working days of the transaction or of detecting it, not 48 hours.

banking_vn_T7.v5: What are the key prudential ratios and lending limits under SBV Circular 22/2019 that a Vietnamese bank must comply with?
banking_vn_T7.v6: What are the key prudential ratios and lending limits under SBV rules (Circular 22/2019, Circular 41/2016 and the 2024 Law on Credit Institutions) that a Vietnamese bank must comply with?
banking_vn_T7.why: The 8% CAR minimum comes from Circular 41/2016/TT-NHNN (Basel II), not Circular 22/2019. The SBV has not made Basel III LCR or NSFR a legal minimum; Circular 22/2019 sets a liquidity reserve ratio of at least 10%, a 30-day solvency ratio and a loan-to-deposit cap of 85%. Law 32/2024/QH15 on Credit Institutions sets the single-customer limit: 14% of equity from July 2024, 13% in 2026, falling to 10% from 2029 (with related persons 21% in 2026, falling to 15%).

banking_vn_T7.v5: SBV Circular 22/2019/TT-NHNN mandates: (1) CAR ≥ 8%, (2) Short-term capital used for medium/long-term lending ≤ 30%, (3) Single customer exposure ≤ 15% of equity, (4) Related party exposure ≤ 5% of equity, (5) LCR ≥ 100%, (6) NSFR ≥ 100%. Violation triggers SBV corrective action. These ratios are reported quarterly and are key CFO/CRO responsibilities.
banking_vn_T7.v6: Vietnamese banks must meet: (1) CAR ≥ 8% (Circular 41/2016/TT-NHNN); under Circular 22/2019/TT-NHNN, (2) short-term capital used for medium/long-term lending ≤ 30%, (3) loan-to-deposit ratio ≤ 85%, (4) liquidity reserve ratio ≥ 10% and the 30-day solvency ratio; under Law 32/2024 on Credit Institutions, (5) single-customer exposure ≤ 13% of equity in 2026 (falling to 10% from 2029; 21% with related persons, falling to 15%), and (6) related party exposure ≤ 5% of equity. LCR and NSFR are Basel III benchmarks, not SBV legal minimums. Violation triggers SBV corrective action. These ratios are reported regularly and are key CFO/CRO responsibilities.
